title: How a Teenager Found Undiagnosed Brain Injuries in the Military
body_text:
Warning: this episode contains mentions of suicide.
New reporting has found that the impact of rough sea waves on rescue-boat crews in the Coast Guard can lead to long-term effects, including traumatic brain injury.
Dave Philipps, who reports about veterans for The New York Times, explains the significant blind spot in the Coast Guard and talks about how a teenager helped expose this widespread danger. 
Guest: Dave Philipps, who reports about war, the military and veterans for The New York Times.
Background reading: 
Rescue-boat crews show signs of brain injuries.
After an article by The Times, the Coast Guard vowed to protect crews from brain injuries caused by rough seas.
